title: Rollout Readiness Checks and Shift Handbook — Nov 2026 (Draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact, shift-friendly handbook for the release window: preflight -> canary -> full rollout -> post-cutover. It combines the readiness checklist, a terse rollout calendar, telemetry/SLO gates we will observe in the first 24h, and quick escalation pointers for on-call engineers. Intended to be printed as a single page for shift leads and stuffed into the release binder.

Who should carry this in their pocket:
- Release lead (primary owner)
- Canary shepherd (observability)
- Rollback lead
- SRE on-call and infra lead
- Customer support triage contact (CS R1)

High-level objectives:
- Keep service latency and error budget within agreed SLOs during canary and ramp.
- Maintain clear, minimal comms: one Slack channel, one Incident bridge, one command doc.
- If any hard gate fails, roll back or divert traffic to fallback model/region within 15 min.

Rollout calendar (UTC):
- T-72h: Final config freeze and release artifact tag. (owner: Release lead)
- T-48h: Preflight dry-run in staging; smoke results posted to #release-ops. (owner: Canary shepherd)
- T-24h: Telemetry snapshot and anomaly baseline capture (compare last 7 days). (owner: Telemetry lead)
- T-2h: Pre-cutover checklist complete; on-call rotations confirmed. (owner: Release lead)
- T-0 (09:00 UTC, 2026-11-06): Canary start — 1% traffic to new build. (owner: Canary shepherd)
- T+30m: First automated canary evaluation (short-window metrics).
- T+2h: If pass, increase to 10% traffic.
- T+4h: If pass, increase to 50% with staged region ramp.
- T+8h: If pass, full rollout.
- T+24h: Full post-cutover verification (end of initial observation window).

Preflight checklist (must be green before T-2h):
- [ ] Release artifact SHA verified in registry and included in release ticket (JIRA-RL-3210).
- [ ] Migration scripts dry-run completed in staging (no schema drift).
- [ ] Canary config (weights, target regions, throttles) checked into infra repo and reviewed.
- [ ] Rollback playbook reviewed and smoke rollback tested (simulated traffic).
- [ ] PagerDuty rotations confirmed and test page sent to the on-call roster.
- [ ] Slack channel created: #rl-2026-11-06 (pinned notes + runbook link).
- [ ] Observability dashboards pinned; synthetic monitors for critical flows green.
- [ ] Rate-limit and quota knobs validated for the new model/variant.
- [ ] Runtime profiling script (for burst analysis) uploaded to /runbooks/profiling.
- [ ] Legal/compliance checklist: data handling flagged? (if yes, do not proceed until signoff).

Shift roles and quick responsibilities:
- Release lead (Lena Park) — single throat-to-choke for go/no-go; call rollbacks.
- Canary shepherd (Diego) — watch dashboards, run manual checks, post interim notes every 30m.
- Telemetry lead (Aisha) — run the automated canary evaluation, own metric thresholds and anomaly explanations.
- Rollback lead (Tomoko) — execute rollback procedure and validate post-rollback health.
- Communications (CS R1) — post customer-facing status updates and coordinate with triage.
- Infra liaison — ensure autoscale and instance pools behave as expected during ramp.

SLO gates and quick thresholds (these are the *minimum* hard gates):
- Error rate (5xx + model error increases) < 0.5% absolute increase over baseline OR < 2x baseline, whichever is smaller.
- P95 latency increase < 200ms absolute OR < 1.5x baseline.
- Successful inference rate (no-ops + model failures) > 99.0%.
- Upstream queue length and worker utilization should not consistently exceed 80%.
- Synthetic sign-in / minimal query flows must succeed within 2x baseline latency.

If any gate trips: immediate steps (aim to execute within 15m):
1) Canary shepherd posts "Gate FAILED" in #rl-2026-11-06 with one line summary and link to failing dashboard.
2) PagerDuty alert to Release lead + Canary shepherd.
3) Rollback lead performs rollback to previous stable artifact (documenting the SHA).
4) Apply emergency rate-limiting (throttle new model) and enable fallback model/region routing.
5) Post-mortem stub created in CONFLUENCE-5462 and follow-up assignment initiated.

Post-cutover checks (T+0 -> T+24h):
- Every 30m for first 4h: quick health post from Canary shepherd (status: OK / Degraded / Failed).
- T+4h and T+8h: intermediate health audit (telemetry lead).
- T+24h: comprehensive audit: cost anomalies, tail latency analysis, user-facing errors.
- T+72h: 7-day trend comparison snapshot for feature flag and routing decisions.

Command & comms primitives (shortcuts to keep comms tidy):
- Slack channel: #rl-2026-11-06 (use only release-related posts).
- Status format: [HH:MM UTC] <role> — <short status line> + <link to dash>.
- Incident bridge: meet.google.com/rl-2026 (auto-record).
- Short template for rollback announcement in #infra-status: "ROLLBACK: rl-2026-11-06 -> reverting to sha: <sha> due to <metric>. ETA restore: 15m".

Quick diagnostics checklist (for Canary shepherd):
- Verify request traces for 5xxs — are they correlated to model server?
- Check KV cache hit-rate changes (prefix cache miss spike?).
- Look for GC spikes or OOMs on model pods.
- Confirm network egress/change in regional routing.
- Check DB connection pool exhaustion traces.

Release notes (internal draft):
- Summary: Deploy model-v3.14 with optimized KV caching and a change to the attention kernel selection that reduces median latency by ~18% in staging. Includes a minor interface tweak: 'response_metadata' added to the payload for downstream logging.
- Why it matters: Improves p50/p95 for short conversational payloads and reduces per-token GPU cost for mid-length (>512 tokens) workloads.
- Known risks: Kernel selector logic is new; edge-case regressions under specific sequence-length distributions possible. We will keep the previous kernel available as rollback knob.
- Customer impact notes: No required client changes; telemetry flagging will surface any client-side malformed metadata.

Open questions / TODOs (owner + due):
- [ ] Final wording for external release note (Marketing) — owner: CS R1 (due: T+24h).
- [ ] Confirm KMS rotation didn’t affect model artifact access (Infra) — owner: Infra lead (due: T-2h).
- [ ] Small perf test: long-seq (>2k tokens) tail-run against v3.14 on an A100 to validate memory path (Perf eng) — owner: Diego (due: T-24h).
- [ ] Add a synthetic that mimics the largest customer prompt in prod (Telemetry) — owner: Aisha (due: T-24h).

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Consider adding a 15-min "quiet window" after full rollout where no config changes are allowed.
- If we see repeated small regressions, prefer divert-to-fallback over full rollback (less customer disruption).
- Save the first failing SHA and snapshot logs immediately (we rarely have the exact failure twice).

Appendix: quick links
- Runbook: https://confluence.internal/redwood/release-runbook
- Dashboards: https://promdash.internal/redwood/rl-2026-11-06
- Canary evaluation job: github.com/redwood-inference/ci/actions/rl-3210
- Rollback script: github.com/redwood-inference/release-scripts/blob/main/rollback.sh

End of handbook. Keep this doc minimal; heavy detail belongs in the linked runbook and Confluence notes.

-- Lena (release lead) — last updated 2026-11-06 09:04 UTC
